primary_claim: AIR, a protocol that uses a sentence embedder to route each SAE/transcoder feature's activation examples to the auto-interpreter based on its category, produces more accurate feature explanations than state-of-the-art auto-interpreters (air scores ~0.73 and air_filtered ~0.87 vs np_max-act-logits' 0.71) while using 9x to 60x fewer tokens.
stated_future_work: have Neuronpedia display a category label for each feature
refine the algorithm used to compute the correlation score and identify a feature's category
train better sentence embedders using the accuracy score of the identified category as a training reward
route obscure features to human manual interpretability or auto-interpretability via smarter models
limitations_stated: AIR can select the wrong category when the correlation scorer doesn't sufficiently penalize genericity, producing a wrong explanation (e.g. the 'big O notation' feature)
obscure features have no correlation or common thread across activation examples or logits, and cannot be meaningfully explained by any protocol tested
quote: `air` with a score $\approx 0.73$ slightly outperforms the best performing state-of-the-art auto-interpreter `np_max-act-logits` which records a score of $0.71$.
